lit.\u0027¿Cuántos puentes de hidrógeno form: "How many hydrogen bonds does a G–C pair form?"
lit.\u0027¿Qué codón es el de inicio de la t: "Which codon is the translation start codon?"
lit.\u0027\u003cb\u003eA–T: 2 puentes de H;: "A–T: 2 H bonds; G–C: 3 → more GC = higher Tm."
lit.\u0027\u003cp\u003eCada \u003cb\u003epur:
"

Each purine (A, G; two rings) pairs with a pyrimidine (T, C; one ring): A–T with 2 H bonds and G–C with 3. All pairs measure the same (≈ 1.08 nm) and that is why the helix is regular. Chargaff's rule: A = T and G = C.

"
lit.\u0027\u003cp\u003eEl \u003cb\u003enucle:
"

The nucleotide is the unit of DNA: a phosphate group on C5′, deoxyribose (a pentose) and a nitrogenous base bound to C1′ (N-glycosidic bond). Nucleotides are chained by phosphodiester bonds between the 3′-OH of one and the 5′ phosphate of the next: the chain has 5′→3′ polarity.

"
lit.\u0027\u003cp\u003eEl ARNm se lee de \u0:
"

The mRNA is read three at a time (codons). There are 64 codons: 61 code for 20 amino acids (degenerate code), AUG is the start (Met) and UAA, UAG, UGA are stop codons. Here the sequence is translated in frame 0.

"
lit.\u0027\u003cp\u003eForma \u003cb\u003eB\:
"

B form: right-handed helix with 10 pairs per turn (pitch 3.4 nm; 0.34 nm between pairs), diameter ≈ 2 nm. The strands are antiparallel and the phosphates face outward. Because they are not opposite at 180°, a major groove (≈ 2.2 nm) and a minor groove (≈ 1.2 nm) form, where proteins read the sequence.

"
lit.\u0027\u003cp\u003eLa \u003cb\u003eARN p:
"

RNA polymerase opens a bubble of ≈ 17 bp and synthesizes mRNA (5′→3′) complementary to the template strand. RNA has uracil instead of thymine and ribose; its sequence matches the coding strand (changing T to U).

"
lit.\u0027\u003cp\u003eLa \u003cb\u003ehelic:
"

Helicase opens the fork and each strand serves as a template: DNA polymerase adds complementary nucleotides (A–T, G–C) in the 5′→3′ direction. Result: two duplexes, each with one old and one new strand (Meselson and Stahl).

"
